title: Quiz yourself
text: Testing yourself on what you've read is one of the best ways to remember it.

title: Brain health and blood sugar
text: Steady blood sugar from regular, balanced meals helps concentration.

title: Avoid long-term sleeping pills for your brain
text: Some sleeping tablets are linked with memory problems in older adults.

title: Anticholinergic medicines and memory
text: Some bladder, allergy and stomach medicines can affect memory. Ask your pharmacist if any of yours are anticholinergic.

title: Stress hormones harm memory
text: Long-term stress affects the memory centre. Relaxation, exercise and support help.

title: Brain-friendly snack: walnuts
text: Walnuts contain omega-3 fats linked with brain health.

title: Eggs and choline
text: Eggs provide choline, important for memory and brain function.

title: Bilingual brains
text: Speaking more than one language may help delay memory decline. Practise a language you know.

title: Get outdoors for brain health
text: Time in nature improves attention and reduces mental fatigue.

title: Do crosswords with someone
text: Solving puzzles together adds social benefits to the brain workout.

title: Craft and create
text: Painting, pottery and sewing combine planning, coordination and creativity.

title: Gentle ankle circles
text: Rotating your ankles keeps them flexible and helps circulation.

title: Finger stretches
text: Gently spreading your fingers wide and closing them keeps hands nimble.

title: Lift with care
text: Get help with heavy items to protect your back and joints.

title: Warm up before activity
text: A few minutes of gentle movement prepares joints for exercise.

title: Cool down after activity
text: Gentle stretching after exercise reduces stiffness.

title: Knees and stairs
text: Lead with your stronger leg going up and your weaker leg going down.

title: Rest is part of joint care
text: Balance activity with rest to avoid flare-ups.

title: Raise a swollen joint
text: Elevating a swollen knee or ankle reduces swelling.

title: Joint-friendly shoes
text: Shoes with cushioned soles and good support protect hips and knees.

title: Sudden joint pain after a fall
text: Pain after a fall, especially in the hip or wrist, should be checked for a fracture.

title: Less knee pain with stronger thighs
text: Strengthening the thigh muscles takes pressure off the knees. Simple sit-to-stand exercises from a chair help.

title: Movement is medicine for arthritis
text: Gentle, regular movement reduces stiffness and pain from osteoarthritis. Rest too much and joints stiffen.

title: Warm up stiff joints in the morning
text: A warm shower and gentle movements in bed before getting up ease morning stiffness.

title: Losing weight eases knee pain
text: Every kilo you lose takes several kilos of pressure off your knees when you walk.

title: Swimming and water exercise for sore joints
text: Water supports your weight, making exercise easier on painful hips and knees.

title: Heat for stiffness, cold for swelling
text: A warm pack eases stiff muscles; a cold pack wrapped in a towel reduces swelling after activity.

title: Supportive shoes protect your joints
text: Cushioned, supportive shoes with a good grip reduce strain on knees, hips and back.

title: Hand exercises for arthritis
text: Gently making a fist, spreading the fingers and touching each fingertip to your thumb keeps hands flexible.

title: Pace activities to avoid flare-ups
text: Alternate heavier tasks with lighter ones and rest before pain builds up.

title: Use a walking stick on the correct side
text: Hold the stick in the hand opposite your painful hip or knee for best support.

title: Pain relief: start with the simplest
text: For joint pain, ask a pharmacist about gels you rub on the joint before tablets. Some are gentler on the stomach.

title: Anti-inflammatory tablets have risks
text: Tablets like ibuprofen can affect the stomach, kidneys and blood pressure in older adults. Check with your doctor before regular use.

title: Hot, swollen, red joint? See a doctor
text: A suddenly hot, swollen joint can be gout or infection and needs prompt medical advice.

title: Gout: drink water and limit alcohol
text: Staying hydrated and cutting back on beer, red meat and sugary drinks reduces gout attacks.

title: Back pain: keep moving
text: For most back pain, staying gently active helps recovery more than bed rest.

title: Lift with your legs
text: Bend your knees, keep the load close and avoid twisting when lifting.

title: Good posture eases neck pain
text: Hold books and screens at eye level and take breaks to roll your shoulders.

title: Stretch your hamstrings for a happier back
text: Tight hamstrings pull on the lower back. Gentle daily stretches help.

title: Sleep position and back pain
text: A pillow between your knees when lying on your side keeps the spine aligned.

title: Physiotherapy works for joints
text: A physiotherapist can give you exercises tailored to your joints that reduce pain and improve movement.

title: Joint replacement: when to consider it
text: If hip or knee pain stops you sleeping or walking despite other treatment, ask about a surgical opinion.

title: Prepare for surgery with exercise
text: Building strength before a hip or knee replacement speeds recovery afterwards.

title: Glucosamine evidence is weak
text: Studies show little benefit from glucosamine for most people. Exercise and weight loss help more.

title: Bones keep renewing — feed them
text: Bones constantly rebuild. Calcium, vitamin D, protein and exercise give them what they need.

title: Prevent fractures by preventing falls
text: Most broken hips come from falls. Strength, balance and a safe home matter as much as strong bones.

title: Osteoporosis treatments work
text: Medicines for osteoporosis significantly reduce fracture risk. Take them as prescribed.

title: Height loss can be a bone sign
text: Losing more than a few centimetres in height may signal spine fractures from osteoporosis. Tell your doctor.

title: Steroids and bones
text: Long-term steroid tablets weaken bones. Ask about bone protection if you take them.

title: Strong feet, steady steps
text: Toe curls, ankle circles and walking barefoot at home (safely) strengthen feet for balance.

title: Foot pain is not normal
text: Persistent foot pain affects walking and balance. A podiatrist can help.

title: Hip stretches for easier walking
text: Gentle hip openers, like knee hugs lying down, keep hips flexible for walking and getting in and out of cars.

title: Shoulder pain and reaching
text: Pendulum swings — letting the arm hang and gently circle — ease stiff shoulders.

title: Rheumatoid arthritis needs early treatment
text: Morning stiffness over an hour and swollen small joints in hands can be rheumatoid arthritis. Early treatment prevents damage.

title: Carpal tunnel: night numbness in the hands
text: Tingling in the thumb and fingers at night can be carpal tunnel syndrome. Wrist splints often help.

title: Keep moving through cold weather
text: Cold makes joints feel stiffer. Indoor exercise and warm layers keep you moving in winter.

title: Gentle yoga for flexibility
text: Chair yoga and gentle stretching classes improve flexibility and reduce joint pain.

title: Massage for muscle aches
text: A gentle massage eases muscle tension and improves circulation.

title: Turmeric in cooking
text: Turmeric adds flavour and may have mild anti-inflammatory effects. High-dose supplements can interact with medicines.

title: Oily fish may ease joint stiffness
text: Omega-3 fats from oily fish may slightly reduce stiffness in rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Don't push through sharp pain
text: Some discomfort during exercise is normal; sharp or worsening pain means stop and rest.

title: Walk on softer surfaces
text: Grass and paths are kinder to sore knees than pavements.

title: Use gadgets to protect joints
text: Jar openers, long-handled reachers and lever taps reduce strain on painful hands.

title: Hydrotherapy
text: Warm-water pools are especially soothing for arthritis.

title: Cycling for knees
text: A stationary bike strengthens legs with little impact on the knees.

title: Knee braces and insoles
text: For some people, a brace or insoles can reduce knee pain. Ask a physiotherapist.

title: Stretch your calves
text: Tight calves can contribute to foot and knee pain. Stretch against a wall daily.

title: Change position often
text: Sitting too long stiffens joints. Stand and move every half hour.

title: Gentle heat for morning hands
text: Warm water soaks for your hands ease morning stiffness.

title: Avoid long periods kneeling
text: Use a kneeling pad and take breaks when gardening.

title: Chair-based exercise
text: If standing is hard, seated exercises still build strength and flexibility.

title: Pain and mood
text: Joint pain can lower mood, and low mood makes pain worse. Treating both helps.

title: Weight and back pain
text: Carrying extra weight increases strain on the back.

title: Back pain red flags
text: Back pain with numbness, loss of bladder control or fever needs urgent help.

title: Neck exercises
text: Gentle chin tucks and slow shoulder rolls ease neck stiffness.

title: Hip pain at night
text: Lying on the painful side can make hip pain worse. Try the other side with a pillow between knees.

title: Frozen shoulder
text: Pain and stiffness that limit shoulder movement for months may be frozen shoulder. Physiotherapy helps.

title: Trigger finger
text: A finger that catches or locks can be treated, often with simple measures or an injection.

title: Plantar fasciitis
text: Heel pain worst in the first steps of the morning often improves with stretching and supportive shoes.

title: Bunions and footwear
text: Wide-fitting shoes with a soft upper and low heel ease bunion pain. If walking stays painful, a podiatrist can help.

title: Ice after a long walk
text: If a joint aches after activity, ice wrapped in a towel for 15 minutes can help.

title: Small swaps, big results
text: Swapping fizzy drinks for water and white bread for wholegrain makes a real difference over time.

title: Watch weekend eating
text: Many people eat more at weekends. Keep healthy habits going on Saturdays and Sundays.

title: Don't shop hungry
text: Shopping after a meal helps you avoid unhealthy impulse buys.

title: Diabetes and exercise
text: Regular exercise improves blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes.

title: Diabetes eye and foot checks
text: Annual eye screening and foot checks are essential with diabetes.

title: Healthy weight and joints
text: Keeping a healthy weight reduces wear on knees and hips.

title: Fibre and blood sugar
text: High-fibre foods help steady blood sugar after meals.

title: Protein keeps you full
text: Protein at each meal helps control hunger.

title: Weight loss after 65
text: Weight loss in older age should be gentle and combined with strength exercise to keep muscle.

title: Measure progress beyond the scale
text: Notice better energy, easier walking and looser clothes, not just weight.

title: Smaller plates, smaller portions
text: Using a smaller plate helps you eat less without feeling deprived.

title: Fill half your plate with vegetables
text: Vegetables fill you up with few calories and lots of nutrients.

title: Eat slowly and enjoy it
text: It takes about 20 minutes for your brain to register fullness. Put your fork down between bites.

title: Watch liquid calories
text: Juice, sweet drinks and alcohol add calories without filling you up.

title: Weigh yourself weekly
text: A weekly check helps you catch small gains before they become big ones.

title: Prediabetes can be reversed
text: Losing a little weight and moving more can bring blood sugar back to normal before diabetes develops.

title: Know the signs of diabetes
text: Thirst, passing urine often, tiredness and blurred vision can be signs of diabetes. Ask for a blood test.

title: Walk after meals for lower blood sugar
text: A 10–15 minute walk after eating helps lower blood sugar spikes.

title: Choose whole grains to steady blood sugar
text: Wholegrain bread, oats and brown rice raise blood sugar more slowly than white versions.

title: Diabetes and your feet
text: Check your feet daily for cuts or sores if you have diabetes, and have them checked yearly.

title: Diabetes and your eyes
text: Diabetes can damage the eyes without symptoms. Keep up with regular eye screening.

title: Pair carbs with protein
text: Eating protein or healthy fat with carbohydrates slows the rise in blood sugar.

title: Unintended weight loss is a warning
text: Losing weight without trying, especially over 5 percent in a few months, should be checked.

title: Being too thin is risky too
text: In later life, being underweight raises the risk of falls, infections and fractures. Eat well.

title: Muscle matters more than the scale
text: As you age, keeping muscle is more important than a lower number on the scale.

title: Keep healthy snacks handy
text: Keep fruit, nuts and yoghurt within easy reach and biscuits out of sight.

title: Plan meals for the week
text: Planning ahead reduces takeaways and impulse buys.

title: Don't skip breakfast if it makes you snack
text: Some people eat less overall with a protein-rich breakfast.

title: Mindful eating
text: Eating without TV or phone helps you notice when you're full.

title: Low blood sugar warning signs
text: If you take diabetes medicine, shakiness, sweating and confusion can mean low blood sugar. Take sugar and tell your doctor.

title: New diabetes medicines also help the heart
text: Some newer diabetes medicines protect the heart and kidneys. Ask whether they suit you.

title: Weight-loss injections need a doctor
text: New injectable weight-loss medicines can be very effective but need medical supervision and keeping muscle through exercise.

title: Sleep and weight
text: Short sleep increases hunger hormones. Good sleep helps you manage weight.

title: Stress eating
text: When stressed, try a short walk or call a friend before reaching for food.

title: Cook at home more
text: Home-cooked meals are usually lower in salt, fat and sugar than takeaways.

title: Limit added sugar
text: Cut back on sugary cereals, cakes and sweets. Fruit satisfies a sweet tooth more healthily.

title: Read portion sizes on labels
text: Nutrition labels often describe a small portion. Check how much you're really eating.

title: Soup before a meal
text: A bowl of vegetable soup before your main course helps you eat less overall.

title: Swap white bread for wholegrain
text: An easy daily swap that adds fibre and keeps you fuller longer.

title: Diabetes: know your HbA1c
text: HbA1c shows your average blood sugar over three months. Ask what your target should be.

title: Eat more fibre to feel full
text: High-fibre foods keep you full for longer.

title: Keep a food diary
text: Writing down what you eat for a week often reveals easy changes.

title: Don't eat from the packet
text: Put snacks in a bowl to see how much you're eating.

title: Swap cream sauces for tomato
text: Tomato-based sauces are lighter than creamy ones.

title: Bake, grill or steam
text: These cooking methods use less fat than frying.

title: Diabetes: regular meals
text: Eating at regular times helps keep blood sugar steady.

title: Diabetes and alcohol
text: Alcohol can cause low blood sugar in people on certain diabetes medicines. Eat when you drink.

title: Prediabetes programmes
text: Many areas offer free programmes to help people with prediabetes lose weight and get active.

title: Healthy weight in later life
text: A little extra weight in older age may be protective, but too much increases joint and heart problems.

title: Fruit instead of dessert
text: Swapping pudding for fruit most days saves calories and adds vitamins.

title: Weight and sleep apnea
text: Losing weight often reduces snoring and sleep apnea.

title: Plan for treats
text: Enjoying a treat now and then, planned, is part of healthy eating.

title: Leave the table when full
text: Stopping when comfortably full, not stuffed, helps manage weight.

title: Diabetes: check your feet's sensation
text: Numbness in the feet can mean nerve damage. Ask for regular checks.

title: Glucose monitoring
text: Many people with diabetes now use sensors that show sugar levels continuously. Ask if it's suitable for you.

title: Bladder diaries help
text: Recording drinks and toilet trips for a few days helps your doctor understand bladder problems.

title: Leaks when coughing or sneezing
text: This is stress incontinence. Pelvic floor exercises often help a great deal.

title: Sudden urges to go
text: Urgency can be helped by bladder training and avoiding caffeine.

title: Pelvic floor exercises — the right way
text: Squeeze and lift as if stopping wind and urine, without holding your breath or squeezing your buttocks.

title: Products for confidence
text: Modern continence products are discreet and help you stay active.

title: Kidney stones and fluids
text: Drinking enough water helps prevent kidney stones from forming.

title: Urine colour as a guide
text: Pale straw-coloured urine means you're drinking enough.

title: Prostate and bladder
text: In men, an enlarged prostate can cause urgency and frequency. Treatment helps.

title: Vaginal estrogen and bladder infections
text: For women after menopause, vaginal estrogen can reduce recurring urine infections.

title: Don't rush on the toilet
text: Taking your time helps your bladder empty fully.

title: Fewer leaks with pelvic floor exercises
text: Daily pelvic floor squeezes reduce leaks for both women and men. Results usually show in a few months.

title: Don't cut down on water to avoid leaks
text: Too little fluid makes urine concentrated and irritates the bladder. Drink steadily through the day.

title: Cut back on bladder irritants
text: Caffeine, fizzy drinks and alcohol can make you need to rush more often.

title: Bladder training
text: Gradually stretching the time between toilet visits can retrain an overactive bladder.

title: Leaks are common, not normal
text: Bladder leaks are common with age but treatable. A continence nurse or doctor can help.

title: Urinary infections in older adults
text: In older people, a urine infection may cause confusion rather than burning. Seek help if someone suddenly becomes confused.

title: Cranberry is not a cure
text: Cranberry products may help prevent some infections in some people but don't treat an infection.

title: Constipation worsens bladder problems
text: A full bowel presses on the bladder. Treating constipation can ease urgency.

title: Lose weight to reduce leaks
text: Extra weight presses on the bladder. Losing weight improves leaks for many women.

title: Night-time urination
text: Raising your legs for an hour in the afternoon can reduce night-time urination caused by fluid in the legs.

title: Stop smoking for your bladder
text: Smoking is the main cause of bladder cancer and the cough worsens leaks.

title: Pads designed for leaks
text: Pads made for urine are more absorbent and protect skin better than period pads.

title: Go when you need to — not 'just in case'
text: Going 'just in case' trains the bladder to hold less.

title: Kidney health and fluids
text: Drinking enough helps the kidneys work well and prevents kidney stones.

title: Double-check your fluids
text: Most people need around 6–8 cups of fluid a day unless advised otherwise.

title: Pelvic floor app reminders
text: Phone apps can remind you to do pelvic floor exercises daily.

title: Overactive bladder medicines
text: Medicines can help an overactive bladder; some may affect memory, so ask about the best choice.

title: Toilets within reach
text: Clear the path to the toilet and use a night light to avoid rushing in the dark.

title: Clothing that's easy to undo
text: Elastic waists and easy fastenings help when you need to go quickly.

title: Indoor plants and air
text: Plants make a room feel fresher, but ventilation is what really clears the air.

title: Breathing and posture
text: Sitting tall and relaxing your shoulders helps breathing.

title: Exercise for COPD
text: Regular exercise is one of the best treatments for COPD breathlessness.

title: Have a breathing plan
text: If you have lung disease, an action plan helps you know what to do when symptoms worsen.

title: Pneumonia warning signs
text: Fever, cough, breathlessness and confusion in older adults can mean pneumonia. Seek help early.

title: Breathe easier with daily walks
text: Regular walking strengthens breathing muscles and improves stamina, even with lung disease.

title: Quitting smoking helps lungs at any age
text: Breathing and cough improve after stopping, and lung decline slows.

title: Get the pneumonia vaccine
text: Pneumonia is serious in older adults. Ask about the pneumococcal vaccine.

title: Yearly flu vaccine
text: Flu vaccines reduce serious illness and hospital stays in older adults.

title: RSV vaccine
text: Many countries now offer an RSV vaccine to older adults. Ask whether it's right for you.

title: Use your inhaler correctly
text: Many people use inhalers wrongly. Ask your pharmacist or nurse to check your technique.

title: A cough lasting three weeks
text: A cough that lasts more than three weeks, or coughing up blood, needs checking.

title: Pursed-lip breathing
text: Breathing in through the nose and out slowly through pursed lips eases breathlessness.

title: Sing for lung health
text: Singing groups for people with lung conditions improve breathing control and wellbeing.

title: Avoid smoke and fumes
text: Keep away from second-hand smoke, wood smoke and strong fumes.

title: Good posture for better breathing
text: Sitting upright lets your lungs expand fully.

title: Pulmonary rehabilitation works
text: Exercise and education programmes for lung disease improve breathing and quality of life.

title: Air your home daily
text: Opening windows for a few minutes clears indoor pollutants.

title: Cold air and breathing
text: A scarf over your nose and mouth warms cold air before it reaches your lungs.

title: Deep breathing exercises
text: Slow, deep breaths into the belly help lungs work efficiently.

title: Damp and mould
text: Damp and mould can worsen breathing problems. Ventilate and treat mould promptly.

title: Sudden breathlessness is urgent
text: Sudden, severe breathlessness or chest pain needs emergency help.

title: Stop smoking support
text: Stop-smoking services and nicotine replacement double your chances of quitting.

title: Second-hand smoke
text: Keep your home and car smoke-free to protect your lungs.

title: Walking with lung disease
text: Short walks with rests build stamina. Your breathlessness should ease with practice.
